answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring a sequential hash thread per identity. Each start value derives from its address and a meadow cell of epoch randomness, so no thread serves two identities. It computes 3,000,000 hashes in sequence, posting checkpoints through a jetty that timestamps them; gaps under 15 minutes are rejected, so the work cannot be precomputed or parallelized, and verifiers can recompute sampled segments. An honest agent spends three hours on one core once. A farm with 1,000 identities needs 1,000 cores for the same 3 hours, since each thread is separate.
